data.content_ref: inline:The proposed diagnostic—justification-evidence linkage in logs—fails to distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere compliance in the single evaluation the problem asks about. A panel can be trained to quote the exact case data point that satisfies a checklist item ('I found X which satisfies the box') without that linkage representing genuine reliability rather than compliance: if the checklist item itself prescribes which evidence to look for, then producing the matching evidence is just a more verbose form of box-ticking. The target's own countercondition (faked justifications copying text without understanding) concedes the diagnostic is spoofable, but the core argument does not show how a single evaluation would separate a panel that understands the linkage from one that merely copies the prescribed text. This is a counterexample-driven gap: the distinguishing evidence the target claims to identify does not, by construction, distinguish what the problem requires.
